design_rationale: This was a cluster-randomized trial: 48 preschool teachers/classrooms were randomly assigned to intervention or business-as-usual conditions, and eligible children were also randomly selected within classrooms.

domain_judgments.rationale: Teachers/classrooms were explicitly randomized and measured baseline characteristics were balanced, but the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods were not reported, and six teachers withdrew after randomization with unequal remaining group sizes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We randomly selected 24 teachers to implement the interactive content-enriched shared book reading curricular intervention and 24 for the comparison condition referred to as business-as-usual (BAU). domain_judgments.rationale: Teachers necessarily knew their assignments, intervention teachers received substantial training and feedback unavailable to controls, and analysis excluded post-randomization teacher withdrawals rather than clearly following intention-to-treat, although implementation and control practices were monitored.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Professional development was not provided because researchers did not want to alter teachers’ typical shared book reading practices.

domain_judgments.rationale: Posttest data were missing for about 7% of randomized children and handled by complete-case/listwise deletion; measured demographics did not differ between completers and non-completers, but outcome-dependent missingness was not ruled out.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All bilingual data collectors participated in a 2-day training with practice opportunities before pre- and post-test data collection and were required to demonstrate 100% mastery on all measures prior to each testing interval.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study reports the stated standardized and proximal receptive and expressive outcomes with corresponding multilevel models, but no preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, leaving possible flexibility in outcome and model selection.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We specifically wanted to know what was the effect of the WORLD preschool shared-book reading curricular intervention and pedagogical approach on proximal and distal receptive and expressive vocabulary outcomes of DLLs in the initial stages of English language development.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The trial was explicitly cluster-randomized with balanced measured baseline characteristics, but allocation methods were insufficiently described, post-randomization teacher withdrawals and complete-case analysis occurred, assessor blinding was not reported, and no preregistration or prespecified analysis plan was identified.

design_rationale: The study explicitly used a computer-based random sequence with assignments placed in sealed numbered envelopes, although one participant was deliberately assigned to the delayed-treatment control rather than randomized.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated sequence and sealed numbered envelopes supported random allocation and concealment, but one analyzed child was intentionally placed in the delayed-treatment control without randomization, envelope opacity was not reported, and the control group had higher baseline expressive vocabulary.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The order of randomization was kept in sealed numbered envelopes... No change was made from the randomly assigned condition for any participant, with one exception... This participant was selected to serve as a delayed-treatment control without random assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and treating clinicians could not be blinded, parental delivery of the bilingual intervention was variable and less intensive than intended, and the analysis appears to include completers rather than all randomized participants after three treatment withdrawals.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: It proved difficult in many cases to keep the parents involved, and this required continuous prompts in many cases... domain_judgments.rationale: Five eligible children withdrew, including three after treatment began, and only completers were analyzed; moreover, home-language outcomes were available for only 21 of 29 completers, with no analysis establishing that missingness could not bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In addition, five children who qualified for the intervention phase withdrew from the study... domain_judgments.rationale: French outcomes were assessed consistently by blinded research assistants with reliability checks, but home-language samples lacked independent transcription verification and MLUw comparability across diverse languages was uncertain.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Posttreatment assessment and scoring were done by research assistants blinded to the children’s treatment conditions... The reliability of their transcriptions could not be rechecked for lack of resources and manpower.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan was reported, and several eligible outcome measures, time points, difference-score analyses, and post hoc tests created scope for selective result reporting despite broad reporting of findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The vocabulary and story retell probes assess skills directly targeted in therapy... These are the main outcome measures of this study, although pre- and postscores are also reported for other language measures.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns. The trial used a computer-generated sequence, concealed envelopes, and blinded outcome assessment, but one participant was assigned nonrandomly, attrition was handled with a completer analysis, bilingual-treatment fidelity was variable, some home-language data were missing or less reliably measured, and no preregistered analysis plan was reported.

design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that 115 children were randomized at the individual level to treatment or business-as-usual control conditions.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although individual random assignment and balanced baseline outcomes were reported, the method used to generate the sequence and whether allocation was concealed were not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The children were randomized on an individual level to a treatment or a control condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and intervention teachers could not be blinded, some classrooms contained both groups with acknowledged potential for diffusion, and an intention-to-treat analysis was not explicitly identified, although fidelity was high and all allocated intervention children received treatment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Among these, fourteen classes ended up having both children receiving the intervention and children distributed to the control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only one child in each group was lost to follow-up, and maximum-likelihood estimation was used to handle missing data, making material bias from missingness unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The analyses of effects were performed with Mplus, version 7.3 (Muthen & Muthen, 1998-2014), using latent autoregressive models (Structural Equation Models) with maximum-likelihood estimation to handle missing data.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were administered consistently using reliable custom and standardized measures by trained research assistants, but assessor blinding to allocation was not reported and knowledge of assignment could have influenced individually administered or scored expressive outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trained research assistants performed the testing, and the tests were administered in a fixed order.

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper reports multiple outcomes, time points, latent-factor specifications, and interaction analyses, but no preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported to rule out selective choice among eligible measurements or analyses.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. Attrition was minimal and outcome measurement was generally strong, but sequence generation/allocation concealment, assessor blinding, explicit intention-to-treat analysis, and prospective specification of outcomes and analyses were insufficiently reported, with additional potential for treatment diffusion in mixed classrooms.

design_rationale: The 28 eligible elementary schools were explicitly randomly assigned to enhanced intervention or typical-practice control conditions; randomization at the school (cluster) level qualifies the study as randomized despite the authors describing it as quasi-experimental at the student level.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although schools were randomized, sequence generation and allocation concealment were not described, five schools were removed after randomization, and the SEI intervention and control groups had a statistically significant baseline difference, raising substantial concern about the integrity of the randomized comparison.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Random assignment was performed among the 28 elementary schools in the district meeting these criteria. Because we encountered a low return rate of parental consent forms at some schools and fewer students enrolled in SEI at some of the schools than initially anticipated, we were forced to eliminate 5 schools.

domain_judgments.rationale: Teachers and participants could not be blinded to the intensive educational intervention, which included additional training, instructional time, paraprofessional support, and parent services, and the complete-case analysis was not an intention-to-treat analysis, although fidelity checks suggested that delivery was monitored.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the present analyses, only those who participated in all three rounds of assessments were included. These students had been enrolled continuously and remained in the same program as their initial placement since kindergarten through the end of first grade.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 534 of approximately 800 targeted students with all three assessments and stable program enrollment were analyzed, the study reports nearly 35% mobility, and exclusions could plausibly depend on intervention and outcomes without sensitivity analyses addressing missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the present analyses, only those who participated in all three rounds of assessments were included... We were not able to study the least stable part of the student population because of a high mobility rate (nearly 35%).

domain_judgments.rationale: The standardized WLPB-R subtests were appropriate and administered identically outside classrooms by trained testers, but assessor blinding to school assignment was not reported and project paraprofessionals who assisted with intervention also assisted with assessments.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective protocol or prespecified analysis plan is reported, and investigators made several data-dependent analytical choices, including compositing two outcomes, revising the model, and conducting multiple group comparisons, although the reported methods are detailed and multiplicity correction was applied.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Therefore, to reduce the complexity of the model, we computed a composite score as an observed variable for each time point.

overall_summary: Overall RoB 2 risk is high, driven by post-randomization school exclusions and baseline imbalance, as well as substantial complete-case restriction amid approximately 35% mobility without analyses showing that missing outcomes did not bias the effect. Additional concerns arise from lack of blinding, departures from intention-to-treat, and no reported prospective analysis plan.

design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that the 94 children were randomly assigned to one of three conditions: business-as-usual control, English-only Literacy Express, or transitional Spanish-to-English Literacy Express.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment was explicit, but the sequence-generation method and allocation concealment were not reported, and some baseline means differed across the small groups without a formal assessment of whether differences were compatible with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Children were randomly assigned to one of three intervention conditions.

domain_judgments.rationale: The interventions were delivered with high fidelity and attendance was similar across groups, but participants and intervention providers could not be blinded to pull-out instruction and the paper does not explicitly report an intention-to-treat analysis or whether all randomized children were analyzed as assigned.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Across interventionists, 90%–98% of the rated sessions received a score of 5, indicating that the intervention was provided to children as intended.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study began with 94 children, whereas each pairwise regression contrast reports N = 63, which may be consistent with excluding the third randomized group but the paper does not provide a participant flow or explicitly account for posttest missingness within each contrast.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Note. N = 63.

domain_judgments.rationale: The literacy outcomes were measured with standardized, generally reliable instruments administered identically at pretest and posttest by trained bilingual assessors who were independent of intervention delivery and blinded to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: These research assistants were not involved in the implementation of the intervention, and they had no knowledge of the intervention conditions to which children were assigned.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified analysis plan is reported, and numerous outcomes, languages, condition contrasts, staged interaction models, and probing analyses created substantial multiplicity and analytic flexibility, with conclusions emphasizing selected statistically significant moderation effects.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 15 significant intervention effects, only four cross-language Initial Skill × Intervention Condition interactions were significant.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because the many outcomes, contrasts, and interaction analyses were not supported by a reported preregistration or prespecified analysis plan, creating substantial risk of selective reporting. Additional concerns arise from unreported sequence concealment, unclear intention-to-treat handling, and incomplete reporting of outcome-data availability.

design_rationale: This was a cluster randomized controlled trial in which 31 kindergarten classes were assigned to intervention or control, with randomization blocked by city, kindergarten ranking, and age cohort.

domain_judgments.rationale: Classes were explicitly randomized within prespecified blocks and baseline characteristics were balanced, but the method used to generate the sequence and whether allocation was concealed until assignment were not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Therefore, instead of complete randomization, we used a blocked randomization process at the class level, blocked by city, the kindergarten ranking, and children’s entry age cohort.

domain_judgments.rationale: Teachers and participants could not be blinded to this behavioral intervention, implementation was incomplete for some teachers, and the analysis is not explicitly described as intention-to-treat, although fidelity monitoring found no control contamination and generally high adherence.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The teachers of treatment group reported that they were able to complete 82–90% of the curriculum plan.

domain_judgments.rationale: Seventeen of 256 children were unavailable at later waves due to moving, with somewhat differential observed retention between groups, but reasons appear unrelated to outcomes and multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses reportedly produced consistent results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Seventeen children in the entry-age-5 cohort could not be tested in the second and third waves of data collection (due to family transition to another city).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were measured identically across groups by testers blinded to allocation and most measures had acceptable internal consistency, but the translated Uyghur instruments were novel and unstandardized for this population, with relatively low reliability for Uyghur expressive vocabulary.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The testers were blind to treatment and control conditions.

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper reports the prespecified-looking four vocabulary outcomes and longitudinal models, but no trial registration, protocol, or prespecified analysis plan is reported, while several outcomes, interactions, covariates, and alternative modeling choices created scope for selective analysis or reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We also fit the Chinese expressive vocabulary (EVT Chinese) models; however, as shown in Model 2, we found no significant differences between the treatment and control groups on Chinese expressive vocabulary growth rate.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns. Random assignment and blinded outcome testing support validity, but sequence generation and concealment were not described, adherence was incomplete, some outcome data were missing, translated measures had psychometric limitations, and no prospective protocol or analysis plan was reported.

design_rationale: This was a cluster-randomized trial because the 25 classrooms, rather than individual children, were explicitly randomly assigned to treatment or control after consenting and screening.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The classrooms were randomly assigned to treatment and control groups at the completion of the consenting and screening process, resulting in 12 classrooms in the treatment group and 13 in the control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Substantial assignment-related deviations occurred because 10 treatment children did not receive Tier 2 instruction and nine received English rather than dual-language instruction; nevertheless, all were analyzed as treated, so the reported effect estimates do not cleanly represent the intended intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Although 10 of the 43 children who were identified as needing Tier 2 small-group support only received large-group instruction, these 10 children were included as research participants because they received part of the intended intervention and the control group received none of it.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome missingness was negligible at 0.65%, and all available observations were included in the analyses, making material bias from missing outcome data unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Less than 1% of the scores were missing overall (18/2754 = 0.0065, or 0.65%), and all available data were used in the multilevel model results that follow.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors were explicitly unblinded, several outcomes were researcher-designed or proximal to the curriculum, and narrative outcomes involved real-time assessor scoring, creating a plausible risk that knowledge of assignment influenced measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Because they were all needed to observe fidelity, support teachers delivery of the intervention, and collect data, they were not blind to assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified analysis plan is reported, many outcomes and repeated measurements were available, and the highest score among multiple parallel forms was selected for analysis, allowing substantial outcome and analysis flexibility.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Six parallel forms were administered, three at pre-intervention (September) and three at postintervention (April/May). The highest score was used for analysis.

overall_summary: Overall RoB 2 risk is high, driven by substantial deviations from the intended dual-language Tier 2 intervention, unblinded outcome assessment with assessor-scored and proximal measures, and extensive flexibility in outcome measurement and analysis without reported prospective specification. Negligible missing data lowers concern in that domain but does not offset the high-risk domains.
